meta.title: Names worth asking about
meta.summary: Scioto, Cuyahoga, Bellefontaine… a familiar-looking spelling can still catch you by surprise. No shame in asking. Local names are an invitation to listen.

sourceRefs.label: E.W. Scripps School of Journalism, Ohio University

blocks.text: Ohio place names carry Indigenous, immigrant, and local histories, and their pronunciations don’t always follow a visitor’s first guess. Scioto is one example: Ohio University’s broadcast guide gives ‘sigh OH tuh.’ Say it slowly, then listen to local speakers; a little uncertainty is a perfectly good beginning.

Pronunciation and origin are different questions, so let’s not turn a spelling guess into an etymology. The university guide is useful for spoken forms; historical and community sources help with the story behind a name. If someone offers a local correction, you’ve learned something. Oops, then onward. That’s how exploring works. ♡
